Institution / endpoint: SNB data portal, cube rendeiduebd (dimSel D0=CHF)
Notes / quirks: SOURCE CHANGED 2026-09-13, and this retires the project's only unofficial source. SPEC.md recorded the SNB curve as discontinued in July 2025; that was wrong. It was not discontinued, it MOVED cubes — rendoblid stopped on 2025-07-31 and rendeiduebd carries it forward, with continuous daily data through the Aug–Sep 2025 window where the old cube ended. D0=CHF isolates Swiss Confederation bond issues; D1 is the maturity, labelled in years-German (10J, not 10Y). Traps: the CSV carries a BOM and two metadata lines before the header and is semicolon-delimited; a query with no fromDate returns only the LAST MONTH, not the full history; and the cube publishes in a MONTHLY BATCH, so a query into the current month returns headers only. That batch cadence is why these rows are judged against a 45-day limit rather than 14. All prior rows were purged on 2026-09-13 (tools/migrate_ch_curve_to_snb.py) because they were OECD monthly averages and TradingEconomics quotes mis-filed under a spot-curve id, and neither could be displaced by appending. This tenor alone is topped up from the SNB interest-rate RSS feed (cb:rateName R10, the same Confederation spot rate, quoted daily), so it stays current between monthly batches while 2y/5y/30y sit at the batch date.

SOURCE FOUND 2026-09-13. SPEC.md recorded ChinaBond as JavaScript-rendered and CFETS as refusing all access; that was true only of the paths tried — the earlier attempts hit the JavaScript FRONT-END. The server-rendered endpoints under cbweb-pbc-web/pbc/ answer a plain cold GET with no cookies, session, captcha or key. THIS IS A SCRAPE and is labelled as one: sturdier than a typical one (official CCDC/PBoC-affiliated, labelled column headers, named curves), but a restyle still breaks it. Parsed by matching the header row by name and the curve by the string 'ChinaBond Government Bond Yield Curve' — the response carries three curves, so matching on position would silently return a corporate curve. Values outside 0–15% are dropped as parse errors. Traps: a query wider than 365 days returns HTTP 200 with a headers-only page, as does a range with no data, so zero rows is treated as failure; and history starts 2006-03-01, not 2010 as first reported. The backfill walks one calendar year per request. Cross-checked against OECD SDMX CHN.M.IRLT (monthly, 2026-07 = 1.71).

Description: UK headline CPI, YoY % and index level
Notes / quirks: SOURCE CHANGED 2026-09-13, off the single BIS dataflow onto this region's own statistics office. BIS releases WS_LONG_CPI once a month in the last week and dates each print to the first of the month it describes, so its newest observation runs 27-57 days old; going direct cuts that. Because the dashboard polls weekly the gain is in AVERAGE staleness, not just arrival lag. Prior rows were purged and reseeded (tools/purge_series.py): the index is on a different base, so appending would have spliced two bases into one series — the exact failure db/quality.check_basis_break guards. NOT one methodology across regions — HICP does not exist for the US, China or Japan — so each region stores its own headline national print and the payload carries an explicit basis. Basis: UK CPI. Deliberately NOT CPIH, which adds owner-occupier housing costs and stops being comparable. api.ons.gov.uk is DEAD (404 on every path); www.ons.gov.uk is the host. Quirks: the months array runs oldest-to-newest, dates read '2026 JUL' not ISO, values are STRINGS, and the quarters/years arrays are different aggregations that must be ignored. ONS publishes 1dp where BIS computed more, so the reseed restated values by rounding only.

Description: CN real GDP, chain-linked volume, constant 2010 local currency, seasonally adjusted (level; YoY/QoQ derived downstream)
Institution / endpoint: World Bank Global Economic Monitor, NYGDPMKTPSAKN (source=15)
Notes / quirks: SOURCE CHANGED 2026-09-13, annual → QUARTERLY. FRED genuinely has no free quarterly real GDP for China (NGDPRSAXDCCNQ, CHNGDPRQPSMEI and NAEXKP01CNQ657S all 404, and the OECD series that used to carry it died in 2023Q3), and the NBS returns HTTP 403 to non-browser clients from outside the mainland — a GitHub Actions runner's exact situation. The World Bank Global Economic Monitor (source=15) carries it: constant 2010 LCU, seasonally adjusted, a LEVEL, back to 1991Q1, keyless, CC BY 4.0, on a host already used here. Worst-case staleness falls from ~15 months to about T+6–8 weeks. LIVE CORRECTNESS TRAP: frequency=Q is SILENTLY IGNORED unless a date range is also passed. Omit it and the API returns ANNUAL rows with HTTP 200, the current year being a partial sum that looks like a real annual figure (measured 2026-09-13: 2026 = 72,551,656 against 2025's 140,133,708). The fetcher always sends date=YYYYQn:YYYYQn and refuses any response carrying a non-quarterly period. The prior annual rows were purged (tools/purge_series.py): both series date a year's first period to YYYY-01-01, so the annual total sat on Q1's date — 134,569,020 against the quarter's 34,475,330.

Description: UK real GDP, monthly index (level; YoY/QoQ derived downstream)
Institution / endpoint: ONS, series ECY2 in dataset MGDP — ons.gov.uk/economy/grossdomesticproductgdp/timeseries/ecy2/mgdp/data
Notes / quirks: Switched 2026-08-28 from FRED's quarterly NGDPRSAXDCGBQ; endpoint corrected 2026-08-29. The .../current/mgdp.csv path previously named here returns 404 — the working endpoint is the ONS time series API, which serves JSON. Observations are under 'months', dated "1997 JAN", so they must be parsed against an explicit month map rather than a locale-dependent format. Confirmed live: ONS carried 2026-06 where FRED's UK series stopped at 2026-Q1, so this is monthly AND two quarters fresher. ONS titles it 'Gross Value Added - Monthly': UK monthly GDP IS the output-approach GVA index, so the description must say GVA rather than plain GDP. History starts 1997-01, where FRED's quarterly series reached 1955 — frequency and freshness traded for depth.

Description: Eurozone real GDP, chain-linked volume (level; YoY/QoQ derived downstream)
Notes / quirks: Corrected 2026-08-29. The dataset previously named here, teina011, does NOT work: it carries only percentage CHANGES (PCH_Q1_SCA / PCH_Q4_SCA / PCH_Q4_NSA) over a rolling 12 quarters and publishes no level series at all. The pipeline derives growth from LEVELS so every region shares one definition (FRED's OECD growth series are discontinued — see SPEC.md's endpoint appendix), and 12 points cannot resolve a percentile window either. namq_10_gdp is the quarterly national accounts behind teina011 and gives the level. Second, independent reason the switch off FRED is right: this is EA20, the current euro-area membership, where FRED's CLVMNACSCAB1GQEA19 is the superseded EA19. Response is JSON-stat: 'value' is a sparse {flat_index: number} map and the time dimension carries {period_label: index}, so the two join by index, not by position. sinceTimePeriod genuinely bounds the response (126 rows -> 6).
Source file itself currently ends 2024-09 — genuine publication lag at Shiller's end, not a fetch bug. Two-row header; match the lower row where col 0 == 'Date'; dates are fractional (1871.01 = Jan).
Use 'Implied ERP (FCFE)' column specifically — 'Implied Premium (DDM)' sits beside it and is a different, materially lower measure (1.69% vs 4.23% for 2025).

Description: UK country risk premium (Damodaran rating-based method — NOT the earnings-yield-implied construct used for erp.US; zero for Aaa sovereigns by construction)
Max history available: back to 2000 (year-stamped archives confirmed 2000-2024; UK is absent from the 2005 file — a real source hole)
Notes / quirks: Added 2026-08-28, implemented 2026-08-29. Stores the rating-based COUNTRY RISK PREMIUM — the spread over a mature market, not a total ERP — so it is 0.00 in every year for the Aaa sovereigns (DE, CH, NO) and is NOT comparable to erp.US, which is the earnings-yield-implied FCFE construct. db/export.py adds the mature-market base (erp.US) back on for display, reproducing Damodaran's own 'Total Equity Risk Premium' column: UK 4.23 + 0.776 = 5.006, which matches the file exactly. Both legs are Damodaran at the same annual vintage. Archive depth CONFIRMED: ctryprem<YY>.xls[x] for 2000-2024. Sheet name moves ('Sheet1' 2000, 'Country premiums' 2001-2011, 'ERPs by country' 2012-now) and the header row sits as deep as row 20, so both are scanned for. Country names carry footnote markers ('Germany [1]') in the 2008-2011 files and are normalised before matching. Values are fractions in every vintage.

Description: US headline CPI, index level (same BIS response as cpi.US, unit_measure 628)
Notes / quirks: SOURCE CHANGED 2026-09-13, off the single BIS dataflow onto this region's own statistics office. BIS releases WS_LONG_CPI once a month in the last week and dates each print to the first of the month it describes, so its newest observation runs 27-57 days old; going direct cuts that. Because the dashboard polls weekly the gain is in AVERAGE staleness, not just arrival lag. Prior rows were purged and reseeded (tools/purge_series.py): the index is on a different base, so appending would have spliced two bases into one series — the exact failure db/quality.check_basis_break guards. NOT one methodology across regions — HICP does not exist for the US, China or Japan — so each region stores its own headline national print and the payload carries an explicit basis. Basis: US CPI-U, all urban consumers, NOT seasonally adjusted, matching every other region here. FRED serves this as a LEVEL only — there is no published YoY series, and the '_PC1' graph suffix is silently ignored and returns the level under the base id — so the annual rate is derived at export from 12 monthly observations. That retired the cpi.US series id. T+11 against BIS's ~T+27. The 2025-10 gap is real: that release was never published, and FRED is missing it too.

Basis: Norwegian KPI, 2025=100. TABLE 14710, NOT 14702. 14702 is CPI by DELIVERY SECTOR and its 'consumer goods' aggregate is NOT the headline — measured 2026-09-13 it printed 7.7 against the headline's 6.5 in 2023M03 and -0.3 against 1.4 in 2020M06, so using it would have published the wrong number for Norway. 14710 is the headline index with no consumption-group dimension to pick wrongly, and 105 years of history — deeper than the BIS series it replaces.
